Cut to tonight's practice. Yesterday was club fair, so we got the usual influx of freshman dregs. It was irritating when another club regular and I had to babysit two nooblets (and destroy them in a dumb game that isn't really tennis), but the match I got was a horribly lopsided one in our favor. At 3-0, I offered giving up one of my serves, i.e., if I hit a serve out, they get a point as opposed to me hitting a second serve, to challenge myself, especially since we have a tournament coming up. I got a stern talking to ("I know it's frustrating that it's a lopsided match, but nothing's really staked on these matches, blah blah blah"). After winning 6-3, the guy talked to me again and said, "thanks for being so laid back, I just want everyone to be happy." What do you mean? I'm frustrated as fuck, of course not everyone's happy, and if nothing's staked on these matches, why can't I take this opportunity to challenge myself?

At this rate, I'm gonna have to start wearing ankle and wrist weights with warm-ups and long sleeved shirts to practice.
